payments.title: Standard Feature
payments.description: Payments is a premium feature available only to organizations on our Standard plan or higher. Upgrade to unlock payment processing and monetization features.

usergroups.title: Standard Feature
usergroups.description: User groups is a premium feature available only to organizations on our Standard plan or higher. Upgrade to organize users into groups for better access management.

api_access.title: Pro Feature
api_access.description: API Access is a premium feature available only to organizations on our Pro plan or higher. Upgrade to unlock programmatic access to your organization's data.

roles.title: Pro Feature
roles.description: Creating custom roles is a premium feature available only to organizations on our Pro plan or higher. Upgrade to create roles with specific permissions.

ai.title: Standard Feature
ai.description: AI features are available only to organizations on our Standard plan or higher. Upgrade to unlock AI-powered content creation and learning assistance.

communities.title: Standard Feature
communities.description: Communities is a premium feature available only to organizations on our Standard plan or higher. Upgrade to unlock discussion communities for your members.

podcasts.title: Standard Feature
podcasts.description: Podcasts is a premium feature available only to organizations on our Standard plan or higher. Upgrade to create and share podcasts with your members.

audit_logs.title: Enterprise Feature
audit_logs.description: Audit logs are a premium feature available only to organizations on our Enterprise plan. Upgrade to gain full visibility into your organization's activities.

certifications.title: Pro Feature
certifications.description: Certifications is a premium feature available only to organizations on our Pro plan or higher. Upgrade to issue certificates to learners who complete your courses.

seo.title: Standard Feature
seo.description: SEO optimization tools are available only to organizations on our Standard plan or higher. Upgrade to customize search engine appearance, social sharing previews, and structured data for your courses.

sso.title: Enterprise Feature
sso.description: Single Sign-On (SSO) is a premium feature available only to organizations on our Enterprise plan. Upgrade to enable secure authentication through your organization's identity provider.

custom_domains.title: Standard Feature
custom_domains.description: Custom Domains is a premium feature available only to organizations on our Standard plan or higher. Upgrade to use your own domain for a branded experience.

analytics.title: Standard Feature
analytics.description: Analytics is a premium feature available only to organizations on our Standard plan or higher. Upgrade to unlock insights about your learners and content.

course_analytics.title: Pro Feature
course_analytics.description: Course Analytics is a premium feature available only to organizations on our Pro plan or higher. Upgrade to unlock detailed engagement data, enrollment trends, and learner progress for individual courses.

boards.title: Standard Feature
boards.description: Boards is a premium feature available only to organizations on our Standard plan or higher. Upgrade to unlock collaborative boards for real-time brainstorming and planning.

playgrounds.title: Pro Feature
playgrounds.description: Plays is a premium feature available to organizations on the Pro plan or higher. Upgrade to create step-by-step interactive activities and badges for your learners.

scorm.title: Enterprise Feature
scorm.description: SCORM support is a premium feature available only to organizations on our Enterprise plan. Upgrade to import and deliver SCORM packages alongside your courses.

webhooks.title: Pro Feature
webhooks.description: Automations is a premium feature available only to organizations on our Pro plan or higher. Upgrade to wire your courses up to webhooks and external integrations.

lti.title: Enterprise Feature
lti.description: LMS integrations (LTI 1.3) are available on the Enterprise plan. Upgrade to launch your courses from Moodle, Canvas, Open edX and other LMSs, with grades synced back.

drip.title: Standard Feature
drip.description: Drip content is available to organizations on our Standard plan or higher. Upgrade to release chapters on a schedule, per learner or for a whole cohort.

paths.title: Pro Feature
paths.description: Paths is a premium feature available only to organizations on our Pro plan or higher. Upgrade to arrange courses into guided journeys with their own certificates.

live_sessions.description: Run live classes, office hours and events with chat, Q&A, polls and attendance.
live_sessions.title: Standard feature

messaging.title: Pro Feature
messaging.description: Messages, course announcements and custom AI agents are available on the Pro plan and with the Enterprise Edition.

company_seats.title: Pro feature
company_seats.description: Onboard companies as customers with their own branded space, exclusive courses and seats they manage themselves.

scim.title: Enterprise Feature
scim.description: Automatic provisioning (SCIM) is available on the Enterprise plan. Upgrade to sync members, managers and groups from Okta, Microsoft Entra ID and other identity providers.

required_training.title: Pro Feature
required_training.description: Required training and manager reports are available on the Pro plan. Upgrade to assign mandatory courses with due dates, reminders and re-certification, and give managers a view of their team.

newsletter.title: Standard Feature
newsletter.description: Newsletter is available on the Standard plan and higher. Upgrade to send campaigns, welcome series and course updates to your learners by email.

review.label: Review this course
review.hint: Quality report, then fixes you approve one by one
review.prompt: Review the course “{{course}}” for quality. Run a full audit, then give me a short report grouped by severity: what is wrong, where, and why it matters to learners. Then propose concrete fixes for the high and medium issues, one change per page, so I can approve each one.

outline_gaps.label: Find gaps in the outline
outline_gaps.hint: Suggests missing chapters and where they fit
outline_gaps.prompt: Look at the outline of “{{course}}” and find what is missing: topics a learner would expect that are not covered yet. List each missing chapter with a one-line goal and where it should go. Then offer to create the ones I pick, with their page titles.

generate_chapter.label: Generate a chapter
generate_chapter.hint: A new chapter with written lessons
generate_chapter.prompt: Add a new chapter about “{{topic}}” to the course “{{course}}”, with {{count}} lessons. Place it where it fits best in the outline. Write each lesson as a full page that matches the tone and level of the existing pages: headings, short paragraphs, an example, and a short quiz at the end.

fill_empty.label: Write the empty pages
fill_empty.hint: Fills pages that have no content yet
fill_empty.prompt: Find the pages of “{{course}}” that are empty or nearly empty and write them. Base each page on the course description, its chapter and the pages around it, and match the tone of the existing pages: headings, short paragraphs, one worked example, and a short quiz at the end. Leave pages that already have content as they are.

quiz_per_chapter.label: Add a quiz to each chapter
quiz_per_chapter.hint: A quiz page at the end of every chapter
quiz_per_chapter.prompt: Add a quiz page at the end of every chapter of “{{course}}” that does not already end with one. Read each chapter’s pages first and write {{count}} multiple-choice questions on what they teach, each with one right answer and a short explanation. Name each page “Quiz: <chapter name>”.

reorder.label: Suggest a better order
reorder.hint: Moves chapters and pages so each builds on the last
reorder.prompt: Suggest a better order for the chapters and pages of “{{course}}”, so each one builds on what came before. Explain every move in one line, then propose the moves for my approval. Do not change any content.

split_long.label: Split long lessons
split_long.hint: Breaks long pages at natural section breaks
split_long.prompt: Find the long pages of “{{course}}” (over about 1,200 words) and propose how to split each one into shorter pages at natural section breaks, keeping all of the content and its blocks. Show me the plan first, then make the split after I approve.

fix_links.label: Fix broken links
fix_links.hint: Empty links, placeholder text and dead buttons
fix_links.prompt: Check every link and button in “{{course}}” for empty or placeholder addresses and leftover placeholder text (TODO, lorem ipsum). Propose a fix for each one: the right address, or removing the link. Ask me when you cannot tell where a link should point.

translate.label: Translate the course
translate.hint: Into a new copy, or in place with approval
translate.prompt: Translate the course “{{course}}” into {{language}}. {{translateMode}} Keep every quiz, block, image and formatting, and translate the course details (name, description, about, learning outcomes) too.

assignment.label: Create an assignment
assignment.hint: Instructions, tasks and a grading rubric
assignment.prompt: Create a draft assignment for the course “{{course}}”{{topicPart}}. Put it in the chapter where it fits best, write clear instructions, add 2 to 4 tasks with points, and write a grading rubric (criteria and points for each task) into the instructions. Set the due date two weeks from today.

announcement.label: Write the announcement email
announcement.hint: A draft only: nothing is sent
announcement.prompt: Draft an announcement email for “{{course}}” for its learners: a subject line and a short, friendly body that says what the course covers and why it is worth starting. Draft only: show it to me here and do not send, post or save anything.

improve_details.label: Improve the title and description
improve_details.hint: Clearer name and a crisp card pitch
improve_details.prompt: Improve the name and card description of the course “{{course}}”. Keep the meaning, make the name clear and specific (under 60 characters) and the description a crisp one or two sentence pitch (under 200 characters) based on what the course really teaches. Show me before and after, then propose the change.

write_about.label: Write the about and outcomes
write_about.hint: From the course’s chapters and pages
write_about.prompt: Write the “about” presentation and 4 to 6 learning outcomes of “{{course}}” from its chapters and pages: who it is for, what they will be able to do, and how the course is organised. Propose them as one change to the course.

tags.label: Suggest tags
tags.hint: Five to eight tags from the content
tags.prompt: Suggest 5 to 8 short tags for the course “{{course}}” based on its content, and propose them as one change.

thumbnail.label: Generate a thumbnail
thumbnail.hint: A new cover image that fits the topic
thumbnail.prompt: Generate a new cover image for the course “{{course}}” that fits its topic and audience, and set it as the course thumbnail.

seo_write.label: Write the SEO from the content
seo_write.hint: Search title, description and image alt text
seo_write.prompt: Write how the course “{{course}}” appears in search and on social media, from its real content: a search title under 60 characters, a description of 120 to 160 characters, and alt text for the cover image. Propose them as one SEO change.

seo_audit.label: Audit the SEO
seo_audit.hint: What keeps it from showing well in search
seo_audit.prompt: Audit the SEO of the course “{{course}}”: its search title and description, cover image and alt text, URL slug, and whether search engines can find it. Tell me what to fix in order of impact, then propose the fixes.

drip.label: Suggest a release schedule
drip.hint: When each chapter should open, with reasons
drip.prompt: Suggest a drip schedule for the course “{{course}}”. Look at its chapters and how long they are, and propose when each chapter should open (for example one chapter a week after enrollment) and whether learners must finish the previous chapter first. Show the plan as a short table with a reason for each chapter, then set it after I approve.

access.label: Suggest access settings
access.hint: Public or members only, contributors, locked chapters
access.prompt: Look at the course “{{course}}” and suggest its access settings: public or members only, whether it should be open to contributors, and whether any chapter should be limited to a user group. Explain each recommendation in one line and only change what I approve.

certificate.label: Draft the certificate
certificate.hint: A title and text from what the course teaches
certificate.prompt: Draft the completion certificate for the course “{{course}}”: a title and one sentence printed under it, based on what the course teaches. Then propose turning the certificate on with that text.

chapter_improve.label: Improve this chapter
chapter_improve.hint: Clearer writing and examples, page by page
chapter_improve.prompt: Improve the chapter “{{chapter}}” of “{{course}}”: tighten the writing of its pages, fix unclear explanations and add an example where it helps. Keep every quiz and block. Propose the changes page by page.

chapter_add_lessons.label: Add lessons
chapter_add_lessons.hint: New written pages at the end of the chapter
chapter_add_lessons.prompt: Add {{count}} new lessons at the end of the chapter “{{chapter}}” in “{{course}}” that continue what its pages teach. Write each one as a full page in the same tone, with a short quiz at the end.

chapter_add_quiz.label: Add a quiz
chapter_add_quiz.hint: A quiz page at the end of the chapter
chapter_add_quiz.prompt: Add a quiz page at the end of the chapter “{{chapter}}” in “{{course}}” with {{count}} multiple-choice questions on what its pages teach, each with one right answer and a short explanation.

chapter_summarize.label: Add a recap page
chapter_summarize.hint: Key ideas of the chapter in a few bullets
chapter_summarize.prompt: Add a short recap page at the end of the chapter “{{chapter}}” in “{{course}}”: its key ideas in a few bullet points and one takeaway.

chapter_translate.label: Translate
chapter_translate.hint: Every page of the chapter, with approval
chapter_translate.prompt: Translate the chapter “{{chapter}}” of “{{course}}” and all of its pages into {{language}}, in place, keeping every quiz, block and formatting. Propose the changes page by page.

activity_generate.label: Write this page
activity_generate.hint: Full content for an empty page
activity_generate.prompt: Write the content of the page “{{activity}}” in the chapter “{{chapter}}” of “{{course}}”. Base it on the course, the chapter and the pages around it: headings, short paragraphs, a worked example and a short quiz at the end. If the page already has content, improve it instead of replacing it.

activity_improve.label: Improve
activity_improve.prompt: Improve the page “{{activity}}” of “{{course}}”: clearer explanations, a better structure with headings, and an example where it helps. Keep its quizzes and blocks. Show me the changes before writing them.

activity_add_quiz.label: Add a quiz
activity_add_quiz.hint: Questions on what this page teaches
activity_add_quiz.prompt: Add a quiz with {{count}} multiple-choice questions at the end of the page “{{activity}}” in “{{course}}”, on what the page teaches, each with one right answer and a short explanation.

activity_flashcards.label: Turn into flashcards
activity_flashcards.hint: Cards for its key terms and ideas
activity_flashcards.prompt: Turn the page “{{activity}}” of “{{course}}” into flashcards: add a flipcards block at the end of the page with 6 to 10 cards covering its key terms and ideas.

activity_summarize.label: Summarize
activity_summarize.hint: In the chat, without changing anything
activity_summarize.prompt: Summarize the page “{{activity}}” of “{{course}}” in 5 bullet points. Do not change anything.

activity_translate.label: Translate
activity_translate.prompt: Translate the page “{{activity}}” of “{{course}}” into {{language}}, in place, keeping every quiz, block and formatting.

activity_quiz_after.label: Add a quiz after it
activity_quiz_after.hint: A quiz page right after this one

mcp.title: Connect AI apps
mcp.description: Let members use LearnHouse from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other AI apps that support MCP. Each member signs in with their own account, picks this organization and chooses read-only or read and edit access. Apps can never do more than the member's role allows.
mcp.server_disabled: MCP is turned off on this server (LEARNHOUSE_MCP_ENABLED=false).
mcp.plans_note: Available on every plan. Tools for features your plan doesn't include stay hidden. For scripts, an API token (Developers > API access) also works as a bearer token.

claude: Open Claude and go to Settings > Connectors.
Choose Add custom connector and paste {{url}}.
Click Connect, sign in to LearnHouse and pick this organization.
chatgpt: Open ChatGPT and go to Settings > Apps and connectors.
Add a custom connector (developer mode may need to be on) and paste {{url}}.
Sign in to LearnHouse when asked and pick this organization.
cursor: Open Cursor Settings > MCP and add a new server.
Use the URL {{url}} as a streamable HTTP server.
Cursor opens LearnHouse to sign you in.
vscode: Run the command MCP: Add Server and choose HTTP.
Paste {{url}} and give it a name.
Start the server and sign in to LearnHouse when prompted.
claude_code: Run: claude mcp add --transport http learnhouse {{url}}
Inside Claude Code run /mcp and choose learnhouse to sign in.

okta.name: Okta
okta.s1: In the Okta Admin Console, open your LearnHouse app (or create an app integration) and enable SCIM provisioning under General → App Settings.
okta.s2: Open Provisioning → Integration and paste the SCIM connector base URL.
okta.s3: Set the unique identifier field for users to userName.
okta.s4: Turn on Push New Users, Push Profile Updates and Push Groups.
okta.s5: Choose HTTP Header authentication, paste the token as the Bearer token, then Test Connector Configuration and Save.
okta.s6: Under To App, enable Create Users, Update User Attributes and Deactivate Users. Assign people, and push groups to sync user groups.

entra.name: Microsoft Entra ID
entra.s1: In the Entra admin center, go to Enterprise applications → New application → Create your own application (non-gallery).
entra.s2: Open Provisioning → Get started and set the provisioning mode to Automatic.
entra.s3: Under Admin Credentials, paste the Tenant URL and the token as Secret Token, then Test Connection.
entra.s4: In Mappings, keep userPrincipalName → userName, and map manager, department and jobTitle to the enterprise attributes.
entra.s5: Assign users and groups, set Provisioning Status to On and Save.
entra.s6: Entra syncs about every 40 minutes; use Provision on demand to try one user right away.

google.name: Google Workspace
google.s1: Google Workspace doesn't push SCIM to custom apps itself: use a provisioning connector or an identity provider in front of Google.
google.s2: In the connector, add a SCIM 2.0 target with the base URL and Bearer token authentication.
google.s3: Map the primary email to userName and emails, and the manager, department and job title to the enterprise extension.
google.s4: Sync users and groups. Suspended Google users arrive as deactivated.

other.name: JumpCloud · OneLogin
other.s1: JumpCloud: in SSO Applications, open the app's Identity Management tab (or add a custom SCIM app), paste the base URL and the token as Bearer token, test, then activate.
other.s2: OneLogin: add the SCIM Provisioner with SAML (SCIM v2 Enterprise) app, set the SCIM Base URL and SCIM Bearer Token, and enable provisioning.
other.s3: Both send the email as userName by default; groups sync to LearnHouse user groups.
other.s4: Any SCIM 2.0 client works: filters on userName, emails.value and externalId, PATCH and PUT are supported.
